content.rendered:
Editing a video normally means installing heavyweight software or uploading your footage to a stranger’s server. These free online video tools take a third path: they process video directly in your browser using WebAssembly, so a clip never leaves your device. Trim, merge, convert to audio, boost volume, change speed, strip soundtracks, and produce thumbnails — with no signup, no watermark, and no upload wait.

Cut and combine clips

The Video Trimmer cuts a clip to exactly the section you want — drag the in and out points on the timeline, preview, and export. The Video Merger does the opposite: drop several clips, arrange their order, and join them into one continuous file. Both are ideal for cleaning up screen recordings and phone footage before sharing.

Fix the audio

Three tools cover the most common sound problems. The Audio Booster raises the volume of a too-quiet video by a chosen amount — the classic fix for lecture recordings and far-away concert clips. Remove Audio from Video strips the soundtrack entirely, which is the fastest way to mute background noise or prepare a clip for a new voiceover. And the Video to Audio Converter extracts the sound as an MP3 — turn a recorded webinar into a podcast you can play in the car.

Change playback speed

The Speed Changer re-encodes a video faster or slower — 0.25× to 4× — with the audio pitch corrected. Speed up a slow tutorial to 1.5× before sending it to a colleague, or slow a sports clip to half speed to study the motion frame by frame.

Thumbnails: grab one or design one

The YouTube Thumbnail Downloader fetches any video’s thumbnail in every size YouTube stores, up to full HD — useful for research, blog embeds and mood boards. Going the other way, the Video Thumbnail Generator lets you design your own: pick a frame from your video or start from a color, add text with outline and shadow, overlay stickers, and export a crisp 1280×720 image ready to upload.

Worked example: turning a lecture into a podcast

You recorded a 40-minute lecture on your phone and want to listen to it while commuting. Open the Video Trimmer and cut the three minutes of shuffling at the start. Then run the result through the Audio Booster at +6 dB because the lecturer stood far from the mic, and finish with the Video to Audio Converter to get an MP3. Three tools, zero uploads — the recording stayed on your phone the whole time.

No uploads: how browser-based video editing works

Video files are big, and “free online video editor” has traditionally meant uploading half a gigabyte, waiting in a queue, and downloading the result — with your footage stored on someone’s server in between. These tools embed FFmpeg, the same engine professional software uses, compiled to WebAssembly so it runs inside your browser tab. The practical differences are dramatic: a 500 MB clip starts processing immediately instead of uploading for ten minutes, your footage never exists anywhere but your device, and there is no file-size pricing tier because there is no server doing the work.

The one honest trade-off: processing speed depends on your device, not a data center. A modern laptop trims and merges near-instantly and re-encodes at roughly real-time speed; a budget phone takes longer on long clips. For everyday clips — screen recordings, phone videos, lecture captures — the difference is rarely noticeable, and the privacy is absolute.

Common video jobs, mapped to the right tool

“Cut the boring first minute” — Video Trimmer. “Stitch these three takes together” — Video Merger. “I only want the audio” — Video to Audio. “You can barely hear the speaker” — Audio Booster. “Mute it completely” — Remove Audio. “Make the tutorial watchable at speed” — Speed Changer. “I need a thumbnail” — grab an existing one with the YouTube Thumbnail Downloader or design your own in the Video Thumbnail Generator.

Working with pictures instead? The image tools compress and convert photos the same private way, and the full tools index lists everything on the site.
